verdict.rationale: Pulumi's own Automation API docs say the engine can 'create, update, configure, and destroy infrastructure,' which is first-party evidence of a destroy capability. The pack never documents a CLI destroy command or a full-stack teardown, so the 'entire environment cleanly' part rests on that single mention. The community note on cleanly deleting k8s resources concerns removing config during updates, not a destroy operation. missing for 10: documentation of a CLI destroy command (e.g. pulumi destroy), explicit whole-stack/environment teardown semantics (dependency ordering, state cleanup, stack removal), independent or hands-on corroboration of clean teardown.
